summary.title: Unleash JavaScript's Potential with Functional Programming
summary.one_liner: You learn the core functional programming ideas in JavaScript (pure functions, immutability, closures, higher-order functions, declarative array methods, function composition and currying), building from primitives up.
keywords: how do i learn functional programming in javascript
takeaways: A pure function returns the same output for the same inputs and has no side effects; these make code deterministic and testable.
Closures give access to outer scope and can provide data privacy, and they enable partial application and currying.
map, filter and reduce are declarative, immutable higher-order array methods, and reduce can implement the other two.
Function composition (compose, pipe) combines small functions and reduces places for bugs to hide; currying turns f(a, b, c) into f(a)(b)(c).
Immutability and avoiding mutable state keep data flow predictable and make programs easier to reason about.
summary.summary: This long-form article walks through functional programming in JavaScript step by step, starting with primitive and composite data types and the difference between parameters and arguments. It then covers pure functions, idempotence, referential transparency, first-class and higher-order functions, and closures. The middle sections explain imperative versus declarative code, immutability, and the native array methods map, filter and reduce, with worked examples and step tables. The article ends with expressions versus statements, function composition (compose, pipe, trace) and currying with a custom curry implementation that uses recursion and arity.
